account: It is ten o'clock, and I am leaving town hall for my scheduled market walk. So far I have no firm evidence of a secret undertaking. The secretary reports no correspondence or town news this morning. Today's appointment book includes tea at three at an unspecified east-bank dockside cottage, with 'the neighbour'; neither the secretary nor I can identify the host from the entry. I asked her to investigate and confirm the address. The same tea entry appears tomorrow, which may simply be a regular engagement, but its vagueness is worth resolving. The secretary also asked where the accounts are kept; I have not established that and intend to check the treasury myself when I return for accounts at one. My last reply was heard by the builder, not evidently by her, so I cannot assume she received it. I saw the builder near town hall carrying a lantern, and shortly afterward a lantern appeared at (-56, -60, 33). This looks consistent with lighting work, though I did not directly see who placed it or learn its purpose. Several townsfolk are gathered near the town-hall road point. I have not yet spoken to them. I should keep my market appointment, hear firsthand news, and avoid treating these ordinary-looking details as proof that anything is being concealed.
